# Incident Report — 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.1.21.58 |
| MAC | 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-ES9F3ML (confirmed via DHCP option 12 and NBNS `<00>`/`<20>` registrations; the same host also broadcasts NetBIOS name WIN11OFFICE — domain computer name vs. local hostname mismatch, not a second machine, same MAC/IP) |
| Logged-in user | gwyatt (Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString`, 10.1.21.58 ↔ 10.1.21.2) |
| Gateway/DC | 10.1.21.2 (MAC 14:b3:1f:2d:ce:69) |

## Malware Family
**Unidentified — behavioral attribution only, not signature-confirmed.** No downloaded binary, executable file name, or file hash could be recovered because every payload transfer rode inside TLS 1.3 with Encrypted Client Hello (SNI shown only as the placeholder `cloudflare-ech.com`), so packet content is opaque.

The observed TTPs match a **fingerprinting-gated malware loader/stealer delivered through a fake file-hosting portal chain**:
1. Fake download portals resolved and contacted in sequence (redirect chain).
2. A large (~16 MB) payload pulled over an ECH-hidden Cloudflare-fronted TLS session immediately after.
3. ~45 seconds after execution, the host begins reporting detailed browser fingerprints (User-Agent, WebGL vendor/renderer, canvas fingerprint, hardware concurrency) to a "set_agent" logging API for two different browser identities (Chrome, then Edge) in immediate succession — a pattern consistent with a bot/anti-analysis check-in gate used by malvertising/stealer distribution infrastructure, not organic user browsing.

Confidence: **behavioral** (TTP/timeline based), not signature-confirmed — flag for a sandbox detonation of any retained sample or endpoint EDR process tree to name the family definitively.

## Indicators of Compromise (all grounded in this capture)

### C2 / fingerprinting check-in
- **153.92.1.49:80** — `whitepepper.su`. Confirmed via clear-text HTTP GET/POST to `/api/set_agent`. Response body is a JS payload that harvests `navigator.*` properties, WebGL vendor/renderer (`AMD Radeon R9 200 Series`), and a canvas fingerprint; the subsequent POST (`act=log`) exfiltrates the collected fingerprint as URL-encoded form data (recovered in full via `--export-objects http`).
- **62.72.32.156:443** — `whooptm.cyou`. TLS SNI confirmed, contacted at t+90s, ~30s before the whitepepper.su check-in — likely a companion C2/redirector in the same infrastructure.

### Payload delivery chain (fake file-host portals, chronological)
- **104.21.22.231:443 / 172.67.207.145:443** — `hiyter.com` (t+45.3s, first domain contacted — entry gate)
- **104.21.48.156:443 / 172.67.154.67:443** — `media.megafilehub4.lat` (t+45.8s)
- **104.21.46.67:443 / 172.67.136.13:443** — `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (t+48.3s; this session carried ~16 MB, the single largest data transfer in the entire capture — the actual payload download)
- **104.21.9.36:443 / 172.67.141.109:443** — `communicationfirewall-security.cc` (t+126.5s)
- **80.97.160.24:443** — `holiday-forever.cc` (t+122.8s)

All five domains resolved to Cloudflare anycast ranges and negotiated ECH, so no real SNI or payload bytes were observable — grouped together on shared naming pattern (fake "megahub/filehub" branding), abusive TLDs (`.sbs`, `.lat`, `.cc`, `.cyou`, `.su`), and temporal adjacency to the confirmed C2 check-in.

### Malicious URLs (recovered in clear text)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log` (POST — fingerprint exfil)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log` (POST — fingerprint exfil)

Bot/campaign ID: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`, token `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`.

### Transferred file names / SHA256 hashes
**None recoverable.** No file name or executable was ever seen in clear text, and the only large binary-sized transfer (the 16 MB session to `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`) was fully TLS-encrypted with ECH. Do not report a hash for this — none exists in the traffic. Recommend acquiring the endpoint (disk/EDR) to hash any dropped binary.

## Benign Context (not IOCs)
Microsoft/Windows telemetry (`*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `settings-win.data.microsoft.com`, `watson.events.data.microsoft.com`, `licensing.mp.microsoft.com`, NCSI `dns.msftncsi.com`/`www.msftconnecttest.com`), Office/Outlook (`login.microsoftonline.com`, `odc.officeapps.live.com`, `ecs.office.com`), Google/Chrome background services (`clients2/4/6.google.com`, `safebrowsing*`, `optimizationguide-pa.googleapis.com`, `mtalk.google.com`), MSN/Bing/Skype, Adobe DTM, Cloudflare CDN/insights (`cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `static.cloudflareinsights.com`), and normal AD domain-member chatter (LDAP/Kerberos/DCERPC/SMB2/SAMR/LSARPC between 10.1.21.58 and DC 10.1.21.2, WPAD, LLMNR, NBNS, mDNS `_googlecast`, SSDP M-SEARCH).

## Incident Summary
Windows workstation DESKTOP-ES9F3ML (10.1.21.58, MAC 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2), logged on as domain user **gwyatt**, browsed a chain of fake file-hosting portals (`hiyter.com` → `media.megafilehub4.lat` → `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`) and pulled a ~16 MB payload over Cloudflare-fronted encrypted-SNI TLS around T+45–48s into the capture. Roughly 45 seconds later the host contacted `whooptm.cyou` and then began reporting granular browser/canvas/WebGL fingerprints to a `set_agent` logging API on `whitepepper.su`, sequentially as both "Chrome" and "Edge," strongly indicating a fingerprinting-gated malware loader or stealer checking in to its C2 after execution. No file name or hash was recoverable due to end-to-end TLS/ECH encryption; family attribution is behavioral only pending endpoint forensics.
